title: Does deep alignment (Qi et al.'s objective) survive RLHF-style fine-tuning on benign data?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: directly tests practical viability of deep alignment for real deployment pipelines that always do further adaptation. If benign fine-tuning erodes deep alignment, the technique's practical value is limited. Immediately actionable finding for practitioners.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Fine-tuning small models on benign data is a well-documented workflow with HuggingFace and the Qi et al. codebase. Measuring KL curves at checkpoints is structured. A beginner with mentor guidance can execute this, though managing fine-tuning runs requires some ML comfort.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable: one model, one fine-tuning run with measurements at multiple checkpoints. Clear metrics (KL depth curves, prefilling ASR at each checkpoint). The output is a decay plot. Well-bounded within 30 hours on a single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Qi et al. (ICLR 2025) proposed deep alignment and showed it resists prefilling attacks. However, the specific question of whether deep alignment survives RLHF-style fine-tuning on benign data is partially addressed: Qi et al. showed benign fine-tuning degrades shallow alignment, and proposed a regularized fine-tuning objective. Multiple follow-up works (BOOSTER ICLR 2025, Antidote, SafeMERGE, SaLoRA ICLR 2025) study safety preservation during fine-tuning. The gap is measuring deep alignment specifically (via KL depth curves) through benign RLHF, which is a narrower replication-style experiment on an already well-studied problem.
